name: Marshall JCM800 2203 Lead Series 100 W Master Volume (1981, 4 x EL34)
description: Marshall JCM800 2203 100 W master-volume head as drawn on the Marshall 'JCM 800 Lead Series 50W & 100W Preamp / Power Circuit Diagram - Standard & Master Volume' sheets (24-4-81) and cross-checked against the Marshall '2203 STD' preamp and output-stage drawings (issue 4-6, 1988), from the input jacks to a 1960 4x12. Inputs: High jack (1 MΩ to ground, 68 kΩ stopper) into the first ECC83 triode (100 kΩ plate, 2.7 kΩ / 0.68 µF cathode), 0.022 µF through the Low jack's switching contact; the Low jack enters after the first stage (a High/Low switch models which jack is used). 470 kΩ ∥ 470 pF into the 1 MΩ log Pre-amp Volume with 0.001 µF from its top to the wiper; the wiper drives the second triode directly (100 kΩ plate, 10 kΩ unbypassed cathode: the cold clipper). 0.022 µF into a 470 kΩ ∥ 470 pF / 470 kΩ divider onto V2a (100 kΩ plate, 820 Ω unbypassed cathode), DC-coupled into the V2b cathode follower (100 kΩ cathode resistor, plate on the V2 rail) driving the Marshall stack (470 pF, 33 kΩ slope, 0.022 µF bass and middle caps, 220 kΩ lin treble, 1 MΩ log bass rheostat, 22 kΩ lin middle with the middle cap on its wiper). Treble wiper into the 1 MΩ log Master Volume, 0.022 µF into the 12AX7 long-tail pair (82 kΩ / 100 kΩ plates, 47 pF between them, 470 Ω shared cathode, 1 MΩ grid returns, 10 kΩ tail, 0.1 µF from the second grid to the feedback node). Global feedback: 100 kΩ from the output transformer's 4 Ω tap into the bottom of the tail, 4.7 kΩ to ground there, and the 22 kΩ lin Presence rheostat in series with 0.1 µF across it. 0.022 µF / 220 kΩ into 4 x EL34 (5.6 kΩ stoppers, 1 kΩ 5 W screen resistors, solved as two matched parallel pairs) at fixed bias (about -42 V), Dagnall C2668 1.7 kΩ output transformer, 16 Ω tap into four 16 Ω 12-inch speakers wired series-parallel (16 Ω). Supply: 4 x 1N4007 bridge (modelled as the equivalent two-diode full-wave) into 2 x 100 µF in series (470 V), choke to the screen node (2 x 100 µF in series, 2 x 56 kΩ), 2 x 10 kΩ 1 W to the phase-inverter node A' (100 µF), 10 kΩ to the V2 node (50 µF), 10 kΩ to the V1 node (50 µF). Standby and power switches closed. Signal cut: the V2b cathode-follower output feeds the tone stack through a one-sample current coupling, as in the 1959 netlist, so the preamp and the tone stack + PI + power stage + NFB loop solve separately.

io.note: outputVoltsPerFS calibrated (2026-11-09) to the mean RMS match gain (-18.0 dB) of the circuit_ab settings against the legacy model, so the A/B sits at the legacy loudness on average across clean and driven settings; final level is a listening-review decision

controls.label: Pre-amp Volume
controls.note: VR1 1 MΩ log between the 470 kΩ ∥ 470 pF network and ground, 0.001 µF from its top to the wiper; the wiper is the cold-clipper grid

controls.label: Master Volume
controls.note: VR2 1 MΩ log from the treble wiper to ground; wiper to the phase inverter through 0.022 µF

controls.label: Treble
controls.note: VR3 220 kΩ linear, wiper = stack output

controls.label: Middle
controls.note: VR4 22 kΩ linear to ground with the middle cap on its wiper

controls.label: Bass
controls.note: VR5 1 MΩ log as a rheostat

controls.label: Presence
controls.note: VR6 22 kΩ linear rheostat in series with 0.1 µF from the feedback node to ground (4.7 kΩ fixed across it): clockwise shunts more treble out of the feedback

controls.label: Input
controls.note: Which front-panel jack the guitar is in. High (on): 1 MΩ, 68 kΩ, first gain stage. Low (off): the Low jack's tip joins the line after the first stage's 0.022 µF (its switch disconnects that coupling cap) and the empty High jack grounds the first grid, so the first stage is bypassed. No legacy parameter is bound (see Hg)

controls.label: Power
controls.note: Stored for presets only. The 2203 has mains and standby switches but no power scaling; the standby switch is modelled closed (open would mute the amp, so it is not bound to a legacy knob)

controls.label: Variac
controls.note: Variac: scales the mains (every transformer secondary, including the bias winding) from 75 % at 0 through nominal at 0.5 to 108 % at 1 (90 / 120 / 130 VAC on a 120 V amp)
controls.modNote: Not on the original amplifier: a variac on the mains, as players did to run the amp at lower line voltage. Offered as a mod; at full scale the amp sees its rated mains.

controls.label: Sag
controls.note: Stored for presets; sag emerges from the silicon bridge, reservoir, choke and droppers

controls.label: Response
controls.note: No part in the 2203 circuit; stored for preset compatibility only

controls.label: Bias
controls.note: Stored for presets. The real amp has an internal 22 kΩ Bias Adjust trimmer (RV1/VR1); it is fixed here (RBADJ at mid) and the bias source is set for about 38 mA per tube

controls.label: Hg
controls.note: No high-gain switch on the 2203 (that is the 2210/2205). The only gain-related selection on the real amp is the High/Low input jack, modelled by 'input_high'; Hg is not bound to it because the legacy parameter's meaning and preset values are unknown here and a wrong binding would put presets on the Low jack

controls.label: G4M
controls.note: No part in the 2203 circuit (no channel, mode or pentode/triode switch); stored for preset compatibility only

controls.label: Stereo
controls.note: Catalogue stereo parameter; the circuit is mono, stored only

parts.label: OT primary interwinding capacitance (plate to plate)
parts.note: unverified: typical-class value, not measured. Physically needed in this model: the transformer part has no interwinding capacitance or core loss, so without it the leakage-inductance current of a cut-off half has only the 470 pF to ground and the hard-driven render rings to kV plates (engine: 502 Newton failures at 220 Hz / 0.3 V with 5 mH; ngspice on the exported deck: 2.4 kV plates with 3 mH). With 1 nF both are clean

parts.label: OT half-primary capacitance (A)
parts.note: unverified: half-primary self-capacitance with its loss as a lumped 470 pF + 2.2 kOhm from the plate to the centre tap (engine lesson from the AB763 Twin: a lossless lumped capacitance rings with the leakage and the NFB turns it into an oscillation; no capacitance gives kilovolt flyback spikes)

parts.note: see CWA

parts.label: Output transformer Dagnall C2668, 1.7 kΩ : 4/8/16 Ω
parts.note: 1.7 kΩ plate-to-plate. Secondary as two windings: common to 4 Ω tap (t4, turns 1/sqrt(1700/4)) and 4 Ω to 16 Ω tap (spk, same turns again); the 8 Ω tap is unused. unverified: DCR 30 Ω per half and 0.2 Ω per secondary section, leakage 3 mH per half (6 mH plate to plate), lm 5 H (20 H plate-to-plate), lsat 2.5 V·s are typical-class values for a 100 W OT, not measured. Secondary phased so the feedback is negative (200 Hz gain 57.3 dB with the 100 kΩ, 62.1 dB with it at 1 GΩ, 69.1 dB with the secondary flipped). Leakage is the loop-stability-critical unknown: with 5 mH per half the 100 kΩ / 4 Ω-tap loop breaks into an ultrasonic burst at 0.1 V input (plates 1.66-1.68 kV in both the engine and ngspice, so it is the modelled physics, not a solver artefact); 3 mH with CPPW is clean at every control extreme tried

parts.label: 4x12 cab: two series pairs in parallel, folded into one equivalent driver
parts.note: Four identical linear driver networks as two series pairs in parallel have exactly one driver's impedance (series x2, parallel /2): folded into one instance, the internal mid nodes sm1/sm2 were never read (2026-11-10).
